method: Unblinded direct visual A/B inspection of all four supplied reference screenshots and all four round-01 candidate screenshots, plus supplied reference provenance manifest. Titles and scene context are recognizable. No builder claims, source code, prior review, or runtime animation inspected.
overall_verdict: FAIL: current output does not win the visual comparison. The Room 4 references clearly lead room and mechanism craft; the Escape Simulator reference leads visible character finish and scene integration. Static evidence does not establish every character/environment finished or autonomous behavior.
largest_remaining_gap: The room focal assets still read as assemblies of repeated primitives with highly uniform materials. The blank door with a torus handle is the strongest example. UI polish cannot compensate for missing dimensional mechanical design, material variation, contact grounding, and authored visual storytelling.

observations: Both bookcases use repeated rectangular volumes and sparse, similarly arranged book blocks. The arch, door, trim and furniture have very simple silhouettes and mostly hard primitive joins.

Wood is strongly orange, uniformly glossy, and visibly repeated across floor, shelves, trim and pedestals; large black ceiling and door areas lack the reference's layered material and silhouette detail.

Reference lighting guides attention through local pools of warm light, shadowed recesses, and material-specific response. Candidate light is broader and objects show weak contact grounding in this still.
room.next_fix: Build one bespoke focal zone around the door: recessed layered panel, beveled frame, inset architectural trim, hinges and bolts, aged metal lock assembly and localized warm illumination. Reduce orange wood saturation and gloss; distinguish floor, cabinet and trim grain scale/roughness. Add darker recesses and contact shadows. Give nearby shelves a small number of distinctive, purposefully composed artifacts instead of more repeated blocks.

character.judgement: Reference wins the visible finish comparison; candidate character is only shown in a small side view.
observations: Candidate robot is mainly smooth cream head/torso volumes with simple tube limbs, gold joints and a flat packed accessory silhouette. The bright cream surfaces separate strongly from the room without much fine material or construction detail.

Reference avatar has readable shaped clothing, cuffs, hands, boots, hair and accessories, with coherent stylized surface response and scene lighting. A robot can meet this finish target without becoming human or photorealistic.
character.next_fix: Refine the robot as an authored porcelain-and-brass automaton: intentional asymmetry, overlapping shell seams, recessed optic housing, engraved identity plate, visible hinge/piston construction, and a dimensional carried tool. Give porcelain, brass, leather and glass different roughness and add grounding/rim light consistent with the room. Supply a face/front three-quarter close view for a real character review.
character.limits: No claims about facial animation, gait, interaction animation, rigging, or unseen characters.

mechanisms_and_ui.judgement: Reference wins mechanisms by the largest category gap. Candidate interface is readable at desktop size but does not establish a finished tactile game experience.
observations: The image labelled mechanism is largely a blank dark door panel with a gold ring, a shelf and a diagram board. It exposes no comparable layered machinery, readable mechanical linkage, engraved control, gauge, or lock state.
The reference workbench and safe use deep assemblies, varied metal treatment, fasteners, toothed parts and a clear relationship between controls and housing.
Candidate UI repeats the title and keeps a substantial investigation sidebar visible during close inspection; the world mechanism has little visual information to compete with that text.

Result capture shows a black exit area with a bright mint frame/handle. It simultaneously displays 8/8 locks open, 6/8 discovered, Opening the exit, and Escape confirmed 100%. This may be an intermediate capture and is not proof of a persistent state bug.

Mobile layout fits the narrow screen but crops out the robot and much of both side zones; small in-world help/status text is hard to read and the lower investigation state is compressed into adjacent columns.
mechanisms_and_ui.next_fix: Replace the ring-on-panel focal mechanism with a layered 3D assembly whose visible controls match the puzzle: engraved dial, toothed moving rings, locking pins, mounting plates, screws, sockets and restrained state lights. Frame it tightly with a dedicated inspection camera and a compact contextual state readout. For the ending, show a designed revealed space/light beyond the door and a stable, coherent terminal state. For mobile, use a purpose-composed camera and one-column investigator state with comfortably readable controls.
mechanisms_and_ui.limits: No interaction or animation quality inferred from stills. No stable terminal-state runtime inspection performed.

next_iteration_priority: Replace the central blank door/ring with a bespoke dimensional lock and surrounding architectural focal zone.
Correct wood material hierarchy and lighting/contact grounding across the room.
Refine and capture the character in front three-quarter close view.
Capture a stable final outcome and compose a dedicated mobile view.
acceptance_evidence_needed: Same reference set and comparable new wide/close screenshots.
A genuine mechanism close view in locked and solved states.
Stable finished ending and mobile view.
Separate runtime evidence for autonomy, interactions and animations; static screenshots cannot establish those.
scoring: No numeric scores assigned. Qualitative comparison only.
